items.Sentence: The headworks consists of one mechanically cleaned bar screen, a bar rack, washer/compactor system, flow meter, a non-functioning grit chamber and inactive screw grit classifier.

The headworks consists of ... a non-functioning grit chamber and inactive screw grit classifier. The City of Guadalupe has reported that they expect to have the grit chamber and screw grit classifier in operating order by June 2023.

Pond 4 can recirculate about 25 percent of the daily inflow back to Pond 2 in the AIWPS system during daylight hours. A 5HP recirculation pump operating at 415 gallons per minute achieves this design parameter.

Treatment train no. 1 is a Swanson advanced integrated wastewater pond system (AIWPS) that consists of one primary facultative pond (Pond 2, volume = 5.2 million gallons) and one secondary aerobic pond (Pond 4, volume = 2.2 million gallons).

Treatment train no. 1 ... consists of ... one secondary aerobic pond (Pond 4, volume = 2.2 million gallons). Pond aeration is required to maintain a dissolved oxygen level at about 2.0 mg/L to suppress odors.
Pond 2 must be equipped with 50 HP of surface aeration (two at 15HP and one at 20 HP) and Pond 4 must be equipped with 10 HP of surface aeration (one at 10HP).

Treatment train no. 2 consists of a Parkson Biolac® Wave-Ox activated sludge with extended aeration system and two integral clarifiers. Alternating anoxic and oxic zones within the bubbled basin are created by controlling the fine bubbles ... therefore achieving nitrification and denitrication.
Treatment train no. 2 consists of a Parkson Biolac® Wave-Ox activated sludge with extended aeration system and two integral clarifiers.
Airlift pumps collect and return activated sludge (a.k.a RAS) to the front of the aeration basin.
A wet weather percolation pond is located after the secondary treatment trains. It has a storage capacity of approximately 43.711 million gallons located on 85 acres.
The solids handling technology is sludge dewatering via a screw press.
There are four alternate sludge drying beds and an emergency sludge storage basin (formerly Pond 1 of the AIWPS system).
Produced biosolids are hauled off to Engel & Gray located at 745 Betteravia Road, Santa Maria, California.
